rules.statement: A public operation that takes a ReadOnlyMemory<byte> (or other borrowed buffer) must document whether it reads or copies the value before the returned task completes, and a value type that keeps the bytes must store its own copy rather than the caller's memory.
rules.why: Otherwise a caller can't tell whether it may return a pooled buffer once the call finishes, and a provider or value that keeps the memory would see stored values change.
rules.check: Look for public methods or constructors taking ReadOnlyMemory<byte>/Memory<byte> whose docs don't say whether the buffer may be reused after the call, and for types assigning such a parameter straight to a field or property without copying (e.g. ToArray()).

rules.statement: In a test project, test each validated bound on both sides: one test accepts the exact limit (maximum, minimum, last valid index) and another rejects one past it.
rules.why: Testing only the rejected side lets a check tightened or loosened by one (e.g. > changed to >=) pass every test.
rules.check: For each range/length/count validation, see whether the tests include an accept-at-the-limit case (e.g. count == Max, amount == 1, index == Length - 1) and a reject-one-past case (Max + 1, Length).

rules.statement: In a test project, write boundary values using the production limit constants (with + 1 or - 1 for the neighbouring cases) instead of bare numeric literals.
rules.why: If a limit changes on purpose, literal-based tests fail for the wrong reason or silently stop testing the boundary.
rules.check: Look for numeric literals in boundary tests that equal a limit defined as a constant in production code.

rules.statement: Make a validation exception's message describe the same side of the bound that the comparison operator accepts (inclusive vs exclusive).
rules.why: A message that disagrees with the operator misdescribes the rule to the caller.
rules.check: Compare each guard's operator (>, >=, <, <=) with its message wording such as 'at or before', 'less than', 'at most'.

rules.statement: An argument exception's ParamName must name a parameter of the method the caller invoked; a factory that computes arguments for another constructor validates the computed result itself and throws for its own parameter.
rules.why: Otherwise the caller sees an error naming a parameter it never supplied.
rules.check: Look for static factories or helpers that pass computed values into a validating constructor, where the constructor's ArgumentException would surface with the inner parameter name.

rules.statement: Put a validation check and its message that recur across types in one internal helper, and declare a message repeated within a type once as a private const.
rules.why: Copied checks and messages drift apart when the rule or its wording changes.
rules.check: Look for identical guard conditions and exception message strings repeated in several types or in several throws of one type.

rules.statement: Pass a capacity when creating a collection whose final count is known, such as new HashSet<T>(items.Length).
rules.why: Sizing up front avoids avoidable reallocations.
rules.check: Look for new List/HashSet/Dictionary created without a capacity right before being filled from a source with a known Length or Count.

rules.statement: In a test project, name a region for a member under test in the '{MemberName} Tests' form, e.g. 'Equals Tests' rather than 'Equality Tests'.
rules.why: Region names should name the member under test consistently across test suites.
rules.check: Look for #region names in test classes that describe a concept instead of naming the tested member when a single member is under test.

rules.statement: In a test project, a test's name must cover everything it asserts; split an unrelated assertion into its own test or rename the test.
rules.why: Otherwise a failure is reported under a name about something else.
rules.check: Compare each test's name with its assertions and look for checks that the name doesn't mention.

rules.statement: Write non-ASCII characters in string literals as C# Unicode escapes (\uXXXX), and when normalization matters, cover both the precomposed and decomposed forms.
rules.why: A pasted accented character's form depends on the editor's normalization, so the test could silently check a different sequence.
rules.check: Look for raw non-ASCII characters in string literals, especially in test data.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask refusal tests to also assert exception message text when each test's input breaks only its own rule; the test conventions assert the exception type and ParamName.
rules.why: When removing a rule lets that test's input through, the test already fails, and asserting messages would tie tests to wording the conventions don't pin.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether each refusal test's input breaks exactly one rule (no other check rejects it) and whether the test conventions pin only the type and ParamName.

rules.statement: Don't report static members declared after the constructor or instance members as an ordering violation: the C# conventions have no static-members-first rule; only a type's shared static instances come before its instance members.
rules.why: The conventions don't require it, and existing code puts static factories after the constructor.
rules.check: Before reporting member order, check the C# instructions for a stated ordering rule and compare with sibling types on main.

rules.statement: Don't ask for XML doc comments to be rewrapped to a column width when the repository sets no max_line_length and the formatter (CSharpier) leaves comments as written.
rules.why: No width rule exists, and a shared paragraph kept as one line stays checkable word for word with a plain text match.
rules.check: Before reporting comment line length, check .editorconfig for max_line_length and the C# instructions for a wrapping rule.

rules.statement: Don't ask for invariant-culture formatting of numbers in exception messages meant for people, such as positive int limits and lengths; the invariant-culture rule covers values meant for machines.
rules.why: Positive ints format as plain digits with no group separator in every culture, and the message is read by a person.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the formatted value is meant for machines (identifiers, protocol, storage) or only appears in a human-read message.

rules.statement: Don't report a method with more than three data parameters when an ADR records the signature, or when the parameters are the operation's whole meaning and recurring inputs are already grouped; the conventions say 'rarely more than three', not never.
rules.why: The limit allows rare exceptions, and recorded design decisions settle the signature.
rules.check: Before reporting parameter count, check the decision records for the operation's shape and whether the recurring inputs are already grouped into types.

rules.statement: Don't apply the no-nested-calls rule to a `new X(...)` constructor expression passed as an argument; the rule covers method calls, and constructor arguments may stay inline.
rules.why: The repository reads the rule that way, and existing tests that follow it keep constructor arguments inline.
rules.check: Before reporting a nested call, check whether the nested expression is a method call or only an object creation.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't require the member-name region form for tests that check a set of constants or the shape of many types, which no single member names; a region naming what the group checks is acceptable.
rules.why: Renaming such regions to a member form would point at a test helper rather than production code.
rules.check: Before reporting a region name, check whether the tests in it target a single production member at all.
